classification.difficultyReason: Update second-draw probabilities without replacement and include both possible orders for one item of each type.

content.prompt:
A bag of confectionary has 27 chocolates and 35 toffees in it.

Sanjesh takes out one item from the bag and then a second without replacing the first. What is the probability of obtaining:

answer.worked:
There are $27+35=62$ items initially. After a chocolate is taken, 26 chocolates remain among 61 items.
$$\begin{align*}P(\text{two chocolates})&=\frac{27}{62}\times\frac{26}{61}\\P(\text{two chocolates})&=\frac{351}{1891}\end{align*}$$

After a toffee is taken, 34 toffees remain among 61 items.
$$\begin{align*}P(\text{two toffees})&=\frac{35}{62}\times\frac{34}{61}\\P(\text{two toffees})&=\frac{595}{1891}\end{align*}$$

Either chocolate then toffee or toffee then chocolate is possible. Add the probabilities of these two mutually exclusive orders.
$$\begin{align*}P(\text{one of each})&=\frac{27}{62}\times\frac{35}{61}+\frac{35}{62}\times\frac{27}{61}\\P(\text{one of each})&=\frac{1890}{3782}\\P(\text{one of each})&=\frac{945}{1891}\end{align*}$$
